1.explanation: The sprite-selector-item component and its container are responsible for rendering each sprite thumbnail and for hooking up the onContextMenu handler that summons the Scratch menu. After a drag-and-drop reorder, that handler either isn’t re-attached or the event is being swallowed by the drag/drop overlay, so the OS context menu fires. The context-menu component itself also participates in positioning and showing the menu, so it’s worth checking there that it isn’t confused by the changed target after a drop. These three files together define and display the right-click menu for sprites, so they must be updated to correctly capture and prevent the native contextmenu event after any reorder.
1.bug_scenario: After you drag a sprite thumbnail to reorder it in the sprite selector pane, the next time you right-click that sprite the Scratch custom context menu (duplicate / export / delete) no longer appears — instead the browser’s native context menu pops up. On first load (before any drag), right-click works as expected.

2.explanation:
• sprite-selector-item.jsx (and its container counterpart) is where we attach our onContextMenu handler to each sprite thumbnail. If the event never reaches this component, our menu never shows.  
• sortable-asset.jsx wraps each asset (including sprites) to make them draggable. Its mouse handlers currently swallow or fail to forward right-click events once a drag has occurred, so the contextmenu event never bubbles up to sprite-selector-item.  
• drag-recognizer.js is the low-level utility that interprets mouse/touch events as drags. It currently treats the right button as part of a drag in some code paths, inadvertently preventing the contextmenu event on mouseup or click.  
• drop-area-hoc.jsx decorates panels (including the sprite pane) with drag-over and drop handlers. It too can intercept contextmenu events on areas where no asset is present, causing the OS menu to appear in the gap.  
• context-menu.jsx is our menu renderer; it never receives the Redux action to open because the right-click handler upstream never fires after dragging.  
All of these files participate in detecting and forwarding or blocking mouse events on sprite tiles. Fixing the event propagation in sortable-asset (and related drag utilities) so that right-click always invokes the onContextMenu logic in sprite-selector-item will restore the custom menu after any drag operation.
2.bug_scenario: When you first right-click a sprite thumbnail in the sprite pane, our custom “duplicate / export / delete” context menu appears as expected. But once you drag that same sprite tile to reorder it in the list, subsequent right-clicks bring up the browser’s default menu instead of our custom one. In other words, after a drag, the onContextMenu handler on that tile no longer fires.
